newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slips to around 3.00/03 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money slips to around 3.00/03 percent.

text.p: German call money rates eased slightly, early on Tuesday to around three percent from near 3.05 percent and money traders expect overnight rates to remain stable.

Traders said they expect the Bundesbank to about evenly match the 68.8 billion marks of repos that are to expire on Wednesday, although there is a chance of a net add to offset higher cash in circulation.
Some also said that the Bundesbank was likely to free repo business from minimum requirements at its council meeting on Thursday.

In Germany, banks must deposit a percentage of short-term borrowing from foreign banks and domestic non-banks in non-interest bearing deposits at the Bundesbank. The requirment is widely seen as a burden on financial institutions and an impediment to Frankfurt's development as a financial centre.

Banks held 39 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Monday, up from 37.4 billion marks. The average for the month so far stands at 39.3 billion marks. Borrowing from the emergency Lombard lending facility was 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= stood at 3.05017 percent compared with 3.05817 percent.
